Red on the LIVE-622 head at its first arm; each later arm mutation-fired. append.detail: CLOSED 2026-09-30 (ADR-1615). RE-TESTED first on the LIVE-622 head (4253506fc): refundCommerceOrder refunded a separate order on the PaymentIntent with no transfer flag and nothing else, so the platform balance paid the whole refund and every seller kept their transfer; charge.refunded reached the same recorders and nothing more; no file called `stripe.transfers.createReversal`; the webhook acked `charge.dispute.closed` through its default arm. SHIPPED. (1) `lib/commerce/split-refund.ts`: the pure `proportionRefund(refunded, splits)` (largest-remainder shares by gross that sum exactly to the refund, each split transfer:gross into the seller reversal, floored so a rounding cent is the platform's, and the platform fee part; a full refund reverses each transfer exactly, a reversal never exceeds its transfer); `reverseSplitTransfers(orderId, refundedCumulative)` writes each row's target first, cancels the unpaid rows of a full refund, plans a partial refund's order the settle never planned, then reverses what is owed; `reverseSplitRefundForPaymentIntent` (the webhook door); `reconcileSplitReversals` (the cron pass). One reversal per owed row: a compare-and-set claim on reversal_attempts, Stripe's own `amount_reversed` read first (a lost write or a dashboard reversal is counted), only target minus that reversed, under the key transfer-reversal:<row>:<from>-<to>. NOT keyed by a Stripe refund id as the brief put it: the refund action, its charge.refunded (whose payload on this API version carries the cumulative amount_refunded and no refund list) and a lost dispute (no refund at all) must derive the same key for the same refund, and the cents it moves the transfer from and to is what all three know. (2) `refundCommerceOrder` branches on `funds_flow`: destination unchanged (both flags), separate refunds with neither, records the refund, then reverses, and a reversal that throws never fails the refund. `recordCommerceRefundFromCharge` reverses on every charge.refunded by the cumulative amount_refunded. (3) `recordCommerceDisputeClosed` + a `charge.dispute.closed` arm in the webhook: a LOST dispute on a commerce charge is recorded refunded for the refunds already on the charge plus the disputed amount through the same recorder, and a split order reversed through the same function; won and warning-closed change nothing. OWNER NOTE: the platform-scoped Stripe destination must subscribe to charge.dispute.closed. (4) MIGRATION 20270345009850_commerce_order_transfer_reversals.sql (authored only, applied to no database by this change): `refund_reversal_cents` (the cumulative target, 0 to amount), `reversal_attempts`, `reversal_owed_cents` generated as target minus reversed_cents floored at zero (the reconciler queue, indexed), and status `cancelled`. lib/database.types.ts by hand; pgTAP supabase/tests/commerce_order_transfer_reversals.test.sql (8). (5) lib/commerce/transfers.ts reconciled with it: a full refund's unpaid rows are cancelled (by the refund, or by the executor when it meets a refunded order), a cancelled row that lands anyway is adopted as created with its whole amount owed back, and a PARTLY refunded order still pays its sellers, whose refund part is then reversed (amends ADR-1614 section 3, which held every row of an order with any refund). (6) The cron `/api/cron/reconcile-transfers` runs the reversal pass after the transfer pass: owed rows under 8 attempts untouched for ten minutes, and `commerce.transfer.reversal_stuck` one line each past the ceiling. (7) NOT A FINANCE ROW per reversal, item 5 of this row: ADR-1614 section 4 removed the payout row a reversal would stand against; the platform fee is already reversed pro rata by the existing recorder. TESTS: lib/commerce/split-refund.test.ts (23, against a stateful ledger and a stateful Stripe: exact-sum rounding pinned across a sweep, a full refund reverses each transfer whole, a partial splits pro rata and a top-up reverses only the rest, a dashboard reversal is counted, a replay through the action, its webhook, a redelivery and a replay past the key window reverses once, a refund before the transfers cancels them and reverses nothing, a transfer in flight during the cancel is taken back after it lands, a failed reversal stops no other seller and is retried once, a stuck one is logged, a destination order is untouched); lib/commerce/checkout-funds-flow.test.ts (the refund reverses after the buyer is refunded and never fails on a reversal error, charge.refunded passes the cumulative amount, a lost dispute reverses and a won one or a destination one does not); lib/commerce/transfers.test.ts (cancelled on a full refund, paid on a partial); app/api/webhooks/stripe/route.test.ts (the dispute arm). Mutation-fired: dropping the target guard, the Stripe amount_reversed read, the cancel, or the cancelled adoption each fails a test. PROBE: red on the LIVE-622 head at its first arm, every later arm mutation-fired.
